label: History
value: Anne grew up at Green Gables in Avonlea.
unit: Anne grew up at Green Gables in Avonlea and pursued her studies with great determination under Miss Stacy. She entered Queen's Academy alongside her Avonlea peers to take the intensive Second Year course, aiming for a First Class teacher's license within a single year. While living in a town boarding house, she experienced acute homesickness, which was eased by weekly Friday trips back to Avonlea. Throughout her studies at Queen's, she maintained a strong academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe, eventually setting her sights on the coveted Avery scholarship in English to attend Redmond College. Later, while attending Redmond College in Kingsport, she lived at Patty's Place with friends Stella, Priscilla, Aunt Jamesina, and Philippa Gordon. During her college years, she was courted by Roy Gardner, though she found herself reflecting on the deeper compatibility and shared humor she had with Gilbert Blythe. Upon completing her time at Redmond, she prepared to return to Avonlea while considering an offer to become principal of the Summerside High School.

value: Anne considered an offer to become principal of the Summerside High School
unit: Anne grew up at Green Gables in Avonlea and pursued her studies with great determination under Miss Stacy. She entered Queen's Academy alongside her Avonlea peers to take the intensive Second Year course, aiming for a First Class teacher's license within a single year. While living in a town boarding house, she experienced acute homesickness, which was eased by weekly Friday trips back to Avonlea. Throughout her studies at Queen's, she maintained a strong academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe, eventually setting her sights on the coveted Avery scholarship in English to attend Redmond College. Later, while attending Redmond College in Kingsport, she lived at Patty's Place with friends Stella, Priscilla, Aunt Jamesina, and Philippa Gordon. During her college years, she was courted by Roy Gardner, though she found herself reflecting on the deeper compatibility and shared humor she had with Gilbert Blythe. Upon completing her time at Redmond, she prepared to return to Avonlea while considering an offer to become principal of the Summerside High School.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye attended Avonlea School.
unit: Anthony Pye attended Avonlea School as one of the ten new students when Anne Shirley began her teaching career. Having previously only had male teachers, he held the conviction that female teachers were no good and treated Anne with scornful disdain. Anne initially struggled to reach him through patience and kindness, finding that his passive resistance worried her and affected the other pupils. Eventually, after receiving a physical reprimand from Anne, Anthony changed his opinion of her. He admitted that she had some worth despite being a girl, noting that the whipping she gave him was as good as a man's.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina agreed to join Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Philippa Gordon, and Stella.
unit: Aunt Jamesina agreed to join Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Philippa Gordon, and Stella at Patty's Place to act as their housemother while they attended Redmond College. She arrived bringing two cats: the Sarah-cat, given to her by her washerwoman, and Joseph, a multi-colored cat entrusted to her by a friend who moved to Vancouver. During the Christmas holidays, she chose to stay behind at Patty's Place to care for the cats rather than leave them alone. At Patty's Place, she kept house, knitted by the fire, listened to the girls' stories, shared anecdotes of her youthful suitors, and offered her pragmatic perspective on writing and romance.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea as part of the Andrews family. After his father deeded him the upper farm in his own name, he sought to get married. Long infatuated with Anne Shirley, his extreme shyness prevented him from courting her directly, so he persuaded his sister Jane to propose to Anne on his behalf during the Christmas holidays. Upon being rejected by Anne, he quickly moved on and married Nettie Blewett. The couple made their public appearance at the Avonlea church on the Sunday following Anne's return from Redmond College, with Billy beaming with pride.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman comes to live with Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Leonora Bowman comes to live with Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge to provide companionship and domestic help in exchange for board and clothes. She is given the nickname Charlotta the Fourth by her mistress, following in the footsteps of her elder sisters who previously held the role before moving away to Boston. During a visit by Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, Charlotta demonstrates the stone house's famous echoes by blowing a tin horn and laughing loudly for them. She forms a deep admiration for Anne Shirley, eagerly practicing before her mirror to copy Anne's walk and chin tilt. When Miss Lavendar grows withdrawn, Charlotta confides her worries to Anne and helps arrange visits to cheer up her mistress. She later assists enthusiastically with the preparations for Miss Lavendar's wedding to Stephen Irving, fussing over minor mishaps and worrying about the weather before dressing in her finest clothes for the ceremony.

She is given the nickname Charlotta the Fourth by her mistress, following in the footsteps of her elder sisters who previously held the role before moving away to Boston. During a visit by Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, Charlotta demonstrates the stone house's famous echoes by blowing a tin horn and laughing loudly for them. She forms a deep admiration for Anne Shirley, eagerly practicing before her mirror to copy Anne's walk and chin tilt. When Miss Lavendar grows withdrawn, Charlotta confides her worries to Anne and helps arrange visits to cheer up her mistress. She later assists enthusiastically with the preparations for Miss Lavendar's wedding to Stephen Irving, fussing over minor mishaps and worrying about the weather before dressing in her finest clothes for the ceremony.

label: History
value: Davy Keith is taken in at Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora are taken in at Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley. Following the death of their relative Richard Keith, a trust fund of two thousand dollars is left for Davy and Dora, enabling them to remain permanently at Green Gables. Davy attends Avonlea School and Sunday School, though he occasionally plays truant or gets into mischief, such as diving off hen-house roofs into straw with the Cotton children or accidentally falling onto lemon pies in the pantry. During a severe storm, he is safely guided home by Anne. Over time, he forms a deep attachment to Anne, whom he likes for 'being you', and regularly confides his childhood thoughts and wedding aspirations to her.

label: History
value: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley
unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley shortly after Anne arrives at Green Gables, and the two young girls solemnly swear to be faithful bosom friends forever. They spend their childhood playing together, building a playhouse in the woods, and sharing imaginative adventures. When Anne accidentally jumps onto Aunt Josephine Barry in the spare room bed during a sleepover, Diana faithfully stands by Anne and refuses to tell on her. Over the years, Diana participates in local community events, including the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and the Christmas Concert. When the Improvers decide to paint the hall, she joins Anne and their peers in dismay upon discovering it was accidentally painted bright blue. Diana supports Anne through various mishaps, such as holding an umbrella for her when Anne gets trapped in the roof of the Cobb duckhouse during a rainstorm and supplying paper for Anne's writing. Eventually, Diana marries Fred Wright and settles down, later giving birth to her first child, a son named little Fred.

unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley shortly after Anne arrives at Green Gables, and the two young girls solemnly swear to be faithful bosom friends forever. They spend their childhood playing together, building a playhouse in the woods, and sharing imaginative adventures. When Anne accidentally jumps onto Aunt Josephine Barry in the spare room bed during a sleepover, Diana faithfully stands by Anne and refuses to tell on her. Over the years, Diana participates in local community events, including the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and the Christmas Concert. When the Improvers decide to paint the hall, she joins Anne and their peers in dismay upon discovering it was accidentally painted bright blue. Diana supports Anne through various mishaps, such as holding an umbrella for her when Anne gets trapped in the roof of the Cobb duckhouse during a rainstorm and supplying paper for Anne's writing. Eventually, Diana marries Fred Wright and settles down, later giving birth to her first child, a son named little Fred.

label: History
value: Following the illness of Mary Keith, Dora was brought to Green Gables.
unit: Following the illness and death of her mother, Mary Keith, Dora and her twin brother Davy were brought to Green Gables to live under the care of Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley. Upon arriving, she behaved demurely, though Davy frequently took advantage of her mild demeanor by taking her food. When school opened, she began attending class alongside her brother, temporarily sitting with Mirabel Cotton. Mirabel's unsettling tales about a deceased uncle ghost frightened Dora so deeply that she became terrified of going upstairs in the dark until Anne comforted her.

label: History
value: In April, Mr. Harrison purchased Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea
unit: In April, Mr. Harrison purchased Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea next to the Cuthbert place, bringing along his foul-mouthed parrot Ginger. He quickly acquired a reputation in the village as an eccentric crank due to his peculiar solitary housekeeping, irregular meal hours, and outspoken criticism of local gossipers. After an initial confrontation with Anne Shirley over a straying cow, he felt ashamed of his temper and welcomed her into his home when she arrived to apologize for selling the animal by mistake. The two shared tea and quickly formed a warm, unlikely friendship, with Mr. Harrison expressing interest in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. He frequently hosted Anne on his veranda for conversations where they debated frankness, human nature, and community matters. In local newspaper gossip, he was jokingly rumored to be pursuing romance, though he actually only visited neighbor Harrison Andrews to play checkers.

After an initial confrontation with Anne Shirley over a straying cow, he felt ashamed of his temper and welcomed her into his home when she arrived to apologize for selling the animal by mistake. The two shared tea and quickly formed a warm, unlikely friendship, with Mr. Harrison expressing interest in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. He frequently hosted Anne on his veranda for conversations where they debated frankness, human nature, and community matters. In local newspaper gossip, he was jokingly rumored to be pursuing romance, though he actually only visited neighbor Harrison Andrews to play checkers.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea as a classmate and friend of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Ruby Gillis. In her youth, she participated in childhood games such as the Story Club and a dramatization of Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, though her practical nature made her hesitant to act in dramatic roles. She joined the Queen's class at Avonlea School to study for her teacher's license, declaring an intention to devote her life to teaching so she could earn her own independent income. While attending school, she wrote romantic and tragic fictional stories featuring heroines in luxurious gowns. In later years, Jane became engaged to Mr. Inglis, a wealthy Englishman with mines, who showered her with expensive jewelry including a large diamond cluster ring. In May, she got married in a blaze of splendor and moved away to travel in Europe before settling into a large mansion in Winnipeg.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis grew up as the daughter of old Mr. Lewis
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis grew up as the daughter of old Mr. Lewis, who named her Lavendar after his wife's favorite scent. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but after a serious quarrel twenty-five years prior, the engagement was broken off, and Stephen left for the United States. Following this, she withdrew into a secluded existence at Echo Lodge, an old stone house surrounded by woods in Grafton. During a trek through Grafton, Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon her house and were welcomed to tea. The encounter led to a warm friendship, with Anne returning to visit and eventually introducing Miss Lavendar to Stephen's son, Paul Irving. Interacting with Paul helped Miss Lavendar reconnect with the past, ultimately paving the way for her eventual reunion and marriage to Stephen Irving.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert travels to Bright River station.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert travels to Bright River station expecting to pick up an orphan boy sent from Nova Scotia by Mrs. Alexander Spencer to assist on the farm. Upon arrival, he discovers a young red-headed orphan girl named Anne Shirley waiting instead, but decides to take her home to Green Gables to let his sister Marilla resolve the mistake. Matthew quickly develops a quiet affection and understanding for Anne, advocating for her to attend events such as the Avonlea concert despite Marilla's initial hesitations. Wanting Anne to have nice clothing like other girls, he attempts to buy dress fabric at a local store, but his extreme shyness leads him to accidentally purchase a garden rake and twenty pounds of brown sugar before enlisting Mrs. Rachel Lynde's help to make a puffed-sleeved dress. Tragically, Matthew passes away suddenly from a heart attack at Green Gables after reading a newspaper account announcing the sudden failure of the Abbey Bank.

Matthew quickly develops a quiet affection and understanding for Anne, advocating for her to attend events such as the Avonlea concert despite Marilla's initial hesitations. Wanting Anne to have nice clothing like other girls, he attempts to buy dress fabric at a local store, but his extreme shyness leads him to accidentally purchase a garden rake and twenty pounds of brown sugar before enlisting Mrs. Rachel Lynde's help to make a puffed-sleeved dress. Tragically, Matthew passes away suddenly from a heart attack at Green Gables after reading a newspaper account announcing the sudden failure of the Abbey Bank.

label: History
value: Paul moves to Avonlea to live with his grandmother.
unit: After moving to Avonlea to live with his grandmother, Paul attends the local school, where he quickly forms a deep bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley. Anne considers him a genius and one of her most beloved pupils, sharing a unique imaginative connection with him. At school, Paul behaves as a model student and gentleman, though he once fought St. Clair Donnell in defense of the Stars and Stripes, resulting in a drawn battle and mutual respect. During Anne's tenure, Paul shares his imaginative tales of his 'rock people' with her and introduces her to his world of fancy. Through Anne, his presence leads to a reunion between his father, Stephen Irving, and Miss Lavendar Lewis, culminating in their marriage. Paul eventually prepares to leave Avonlea to live in Boston with his father and new stepmother, Miss Lavendar.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon was raised in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Philippa Gordon was raised in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, as the daughter of a prominent family. Upon entering Redmond College in Kingsport, she met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in Old St. John's Cemetery during her first days of school, quickly declaring her desire to be chummy with them. Her charm and social status granted her access to all Redmond circles, and she brought Anne and Priscilla along into her expanding social life. While at college, she balanced a crowded social life and numerous suitors, including Alec and Alonzo from home, with her academic studies. During her visits home to Mount Holly in Bolingbroke, she hosted continuous social gatherings for her friends.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for decades in Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea with her husband Thomas. When Matthew Cuthbert brought orphan Anne Shirley to Green Gables, Rachel visited and criticized Anne's freckles and red hair, provoking an explosive outburst from the child. Though offended, she eventually accepted Anne's apology. Over the years, she maintained an active role in Avonlea's local affairs, soliciting funds for church carpets and keeping close watch on neighborhood activities. When her husband Thomas fell gravely ill, she nursed him tenderly until his peaceful death. Facing financial difficulties due to a mortgaged farm and medical bills, she expected to leave Avonlea until Marilla Cuthbert invited her to move into Green Gables. Rachel accepted the offer, relocating to the north gable and spare room of Green Gables while helping Marilla care for the young Keith twins.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner interrupted his college studies.
unit: Roy Gardner interrupted his college studies for two years to travel abroad with his ailing mother. Upon returning, he rescued Anne Shirley in a park during a rainstorm when her umbrella turned inside out, subsequently sending her long-stemmed roses and courting her. Over two years, he regularly visited Patty's Place, brought Anne flowers, and escorted her to Redmond events, winning the high regard of Aunt Jamesina and her friends. He took Anne to a harbor shore pavilion where they had first talked to propose to her with a eloquently prepared speech. However, Anne unexpectedly refused his proposal because she did not care enough for him, leaving Roy heartbroken, disappointed, and bitter over the end of their relationship.

unit: Roy Gardner interrupted his college studies for two years to travel abroad with his ailing mother. Upon returning, he rescued Anne Shirley in a park during a rainstorm when her umbrella turned inside out, subsequently sending her long-stemmed roses and courting her. Over two years, he regularly visited Patty's Place, brought Anne flowers, and escorted her to Redmond events, winning the high regard of Aunt Jamesina and her friends. He took Anne to a harbor shore pavilion where they had first talked to propose to her with a eloquently prepared speech. However, Anne unexpectedly refused his proposal because she did not care enough for him, leaving Roy heartbroken, disappointed, and bitter over the end of their relationship.

value: Ruby is a showy girl.
unit: Ruby is a showy, handsome girl with a fair complexion and blue eyes. She has long, lovely golden hair worn in braids. During her fatal illness, her cheeks are hectically brilliant, her eyes grow overly bright, and her body becomes very thin.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea as part of a circle of schoolmates including Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews. As a young girl, she participated in outdoor play, such as dramatizing Tennyson's Elaine on the pond. She later attended Queen's Academy alongside her friends. After entering the teaching profession, she fell ill with a severe attack of congestion during the winter, preventing her from continuing her duties. Despite her declining health from galloping consumption, Ruby remained hopeful, pursuing the White Sands school teaching position and continuing her social life with suitors like Herb Spencer. Eventually, her strength failed and she had to give up teaching. One evening in her garden, she confessed her terrifying awareness of her approaching death to Anne. She passed away quietly in her sleep the following night and was laid to rest in the Avonlea graveyard.

After entering the teaching profession, she fell ill with a severe attack of congestion during the winter, preventing her from continuing her duties. Despite her declining health from galloping consumption, Ruby remained hopeful, pursuing the White Sands school teaching position and continuing her social life with suitors like Herb Spencer. Eventually, her strength failed and she had to give up teaching. One evening in her garden, she confessed her terrifying awareness of her approaching death to Anne. She passed away quietly in her sleep the following night and was laid to rest in the Avonlea graveyard.

value: Stacy served as the teacher
unit: Miss Stacy served as the teacher at Avonlea school. When she caught Anne Shirley reading a novel hidden behind her textbook in class, she kept Anne in at recess to explain why deceit was wrong and forgave her warmly. Recognizing the potential of her advanced pupils, Miss Stacy organized an extra class after school to help prepare them for the Queen's Academy Entrance examinations, seeking permission from their guardians. Although she was offered a position in her home district's grade school, she chose to return to Avonlea because of her strong attachment to her students. At the end of the school term, she encouraged her pupils to rest and avoid studying during the exam week, personally accompanying them to the Academy on the day of their tests.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, becoming one of their close chums. After graduating, she spent two years teaching in a rural country school with nine grades, an experience she found exasperating due to low pay, demanding parents, and public misconceptions about the work. Tired of teaching and boarding, she decided to resign and enter Redmond College as a Sophomore. She devised a plan to rent a house in Kingsport called Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, and later Philippa Gordon, enlisting her aunt, Aunt Jamesina, to move in as their housekeeper. While residing at Patty's Place during her college years, Stella focused on her studies and shared household life with her friends and their pets.

unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, becoming one of their close chums. After graduating, she spent two years teaching in a rural country school with nine grades, an experience she found exasperating due to low pay, demanding parents, and public misconceptions about the work. Tired of teaching and boarding, she decided to resign and enter Redmond College as a Sophomore. She devised a plan to rent a house in Kingsport called Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, and later Philippa Gordon, enlisting her aunt, Aunt Jamesina, to move in as their housekeeper. While residing at Patty's Place during her college years, Stella focused on her studies and shared household life with her friends and their pets.
